conflicts.description: Switch 44 (Past Crane) is opto-constructed per the manual's Switch Locations parts list (2-35), which prints an A-16908 (LED) / A-16909 (PHOTO TRANS) opto pair for item 44 as it does for items 41-43 -- but pinned PinMAME's jyGameData inverted-switch mask ({0x00,0x00,0x00,0x7f,0x07,0x00,0x00,...}) covers column 4 rows 1-3 (0x07, switches 41-43) and leaves row 4 (switch 44) uninverted. The other ten opto addresses (31-37, 41-43) all agree between the manual and the emulator; this is the sole polarity disagreement, of the same family as Monster Bash's Dracula-position optos and Indiana Jones's captive-ball opto. Resolution path: a LibPinMAME gameplay-harness trace of a legal jy_11/jy_12 ROM observing the public idle state of switch 44 and its transitions as the crane passes, or a later corrected upstream mask.

Lamp 86 (Gen. Crane) sits on an unresolved physical plane. The manual's own Lamp Locations page (2-37) disagrees with itself: the footnote asterisks items 81-86 as "located on the insert panel", but the same page's playfield line drawing runs a leader from a margin badge 86 into the on-playfield crane mechanism at the top of the playfield. The retained table models a Lamp86 Light object on the playfield, which agrees with the drawing's crane placement but not with the insert-panel footnote. The transcription records both facts without picking a side. The definition places lamp 86 on the playfield from the retained table and notes the conflict. Resolution path: a photograph of an unrestored machine with the Gen. Crane lamp lit, or the insert-panel/crane assembly lamp wiring, to confirm which physical plane the #44 socket sits on.

drivers.variant_notes: Williams production 1.2 game ROM (DCS sound) shipped with the physical machine; the retained known-working script binds this exact driver (cGameName = "jy_12"). Pinned PinMAME's own libpinmame.h comment names GEN_WPC95 "Integrated boards, Congo 3/96 - Cactus Canyon 2/99", i.e. Junk Yard is part of the same integrated-board WPC-95 hardware generation as the other machines in that era.

Williams 1.2C Competition MOD (2019), a community ruleset built on the 1.2 game ROM that runs on the identical physical hardware and addresses; a later firmware revision of the same physical machine with no controller-address or playfield change.
Williams 1.1 game ROM; an earlier firmware revision of the same physical machine with no controller-address or playfield change.
Williams 0.3 Prototype game ROM; a prototype firmware revision of the same physical machine with no controller-address or playfield change.

physical.notes: Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F1. PinMAME forces this end-of-stroke address every VBLANK: jyGameData's FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L) sets the lower-flipper FLIP_EOS bit, so core_updateSw recomputes it from core_getSol (the flipper hold coil state) plus CORE_FLIPSTROKETIME and writes it back into the matrix. A recreation must not drive it. Its normalized coordinate is the retained table's own flipper pivot center: the retained extraction contains no separate EOS contact object, so this is a documented projection onto the flipper assembly rather than a surveyed sensor position.

Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F2. The switch matrix's Fliptronic block shades this position as an opto that is typically closed. WPC-95 reads the flipper column through WPC_FLIPPERSW95 with a hardware inversion, so the public switch state is already normalized.

Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F3. PinMAME forces this end-of-stroke address every VBLANK: jyGameData's FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L) sets the lower-flipper FLIP_EOS bit, so core_updateSw recomputes it from core_getSol (the flipper hold coil state) plus CORE_FLIPSTROKETIME and writes it back into the matrix. A recreation must not drive it. Its normalized coordinate is the retained table's own flipper pivot center: the retained extraction contains no separate EOS contact object, so this is a documented projection onto the flipper assembly rather than a surveyed sensor position.

Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F5.

inputs.label: Not Fitted Upper Right Flipper Button

physical.notes: Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F6. Junk Yard fits no upper flippers, so no physical upper-flipper button is installed (the Switch Locations page prints this position Not Used). jyGameData's FLIP_SW(FLIP_L | FLIP_U) includes the FLIP_U bit, so PinMAME's flipMask carries the upper-flipper button bit, but under LibPinMAME (g_fHandleKeyboard=0) the button bits are read straight from and written back to the matrix unchanged, so PinMAME publishes no meaningful runtime state at this address. (In keyboard mode core.c copies the lower-flipper key state into these bits because FLIP_BUT(FLIP_UR/UL) is unset, mirroring the FunHouse pattern.) Recorded unused.

inputs.label: Not Used Upper Left Flipper EOS

physical.notes: Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F7. mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest on trough optos 32-35; the retained script's cvpmTrough helper (bsTrough) reads them as a plain switch array [32,33,34,35] and ejects the ball nearest the shooter lane through solenoid 9 (Trough), pulsing trough-eject opto 31 in the same SolTrough event. All five positions are printed optos that rest closed, normalized by PinMAME's column-3 inverted-switch mask bits.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough and ball release

positions.description: Opto pulsed as the ejected ball leaves.
positions.label: Trough eject

mechanisms.behavior: The ball ejected from the trough rests on shooter-lane switch 18 and auto-plunger coil 1 launches it; the retained script's Autoplunger handler pulls back and fires the Auto_Plunger only when switch 18 is active.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and auto plunger

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 3 (Power Crane) drives the crane arm that raises and swings the wrecking-ball head across the top of the playfield; solenoid 15 (Hold Crane) holds the mechanism against gravity. The retained script's SolPowerCrane/SolHoldCrane handlers steer the Wrecker ball along the crane track while switch 15 (Top Left Crane) and 44 (Past Crane) report the arm's positional limits and switch 28 (Crane Down) reports the lowered position.
mechanisms.label: Crane mechanism with wrecking ball

positions.description: Crane head at the left stop.
positions.label: Top Left Crane position

positions.description: Crane head past the right stop.
positions.label: Past Crane position

mechanisms.behavior: The retained script's second cvpmBallStack helper (bsFridgePopper) uses switch 37 as its entry ball-position switch and switches 36/43 as the Fridge ball-stack array; solenoid 2 fires the popper to eject a captured ball back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Refrigerator popper

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 6 rotates a diverter flap (Sol6, a stopping wall/diverter object) that selects whether a ball entering the bus ramp lane continues to the top of the playfield or drops back; the retained script's BusDiverter handler sets Sol6.IsDropped accordingly. The manual documents no dedicated switch for this device.
mechanisms.label: Bus ramp diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 16 (Move Dog) drives the dog-house spike arm; the retained script's SpikeBark/SpikeTimer handlers pulse the spike spike.transy up and down while switch 74 (Dog Entry) reports a ball in the dog-house entry scoop.
mechanisms.label: Spike the dog mechanism

mechanisms.behavior: The two-way fork-lift scoop at the center-right of the playfield lowers (solenoid 5, Scoop Down) and raises (solenoid 21, Scoop Up) to fling a ball from switch 73 (Scoop Made); the retained script's ScoopDown/ScoopUp handlers drive the fork-arm primitives and toggle switch 72 to report the scoop's own state.
mechanisms.label: Fork-lift scoop (up/down)

positions.description: State switch toggled by the ScoopDown handler.
positions.label: Scoop lowered

mechanisms.behavior: Toaster Gun (switch 11) and Rebound Switch (switch 12, part A-17794) form the left-side upper features; the retained script pulses switch 12 from both the Switch12 and Switch12a wall hit handlers.
mechanisms.label: Toaster gun and rebound

mechanisms.behavior: Five standup targets (Car Target 1-5) sit at the top of the playfield above the crane track (SW-1A-210-1 through -5); they are hit targets, not a resettable drop bank.
mechanisms.label: Car drop-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: Four clusters of three standup targets each: Upper Right 3-Bank (61-63), Upper Left 3-Bank (64-66), Lower Left 3-Bank (56-58) and Right 3-Bank (76-78). All use part A-21349-1 (lower/right clusters) or A-21351-1..-6 (upper clusters).
mechanisms.label: Upper and lower three-bank target clusters

mechanisms.behavior: Each slingshot assembly has a combined kick/score switch (SW-1A-204 kick with SW-1A-205 score); the retained script's LeftSlingShot_Slingshot/RightSlingShot_Slingshot handlers pulse switches 51 and 52 while coils 10/11 articulate the arms.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: The Fliptronic F5 position is a playfield spinner (part 5647-12693-24), not a flipper contact; the retained script's Switch115_Spin handler pulses switch 115 on each revolution.
mechanisms.label: Spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Two FL-11629 flippers on Fliptronic circuits. Each flipper has a separate power and hold winding: the ROM energizes the power winding on the cabinet button opto (112 right, 114 left), then drops to the hold winding once the end-of-stroke leaf switch (111 right, 113 left) closes. Printed circuits 29/30 (Lwr Rt Power/Hold) and 31/32 (Lwr Lt Power/Hold) map to public addresses 45-48.
mechanisms.label: Lower flipper pair

physical.notes: Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 01 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: Autoplunger (Auto_Plunger.Pullback/.Fire when switch 18).
Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 02 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: bsFridgePopper.SolOut.

Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 03 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: SolPowerCrane (Wrecker ball chain/crane drive). Projected onto the crane mechanism's top-left hole (Kicker CraneHole, table object center); the crane arm itself (PCraneArm) is a render primitive without a switch/solenoid collision object. Note the manual's Solenoid Locations drawing places the Power Crane callout top-right-of-center at the crane assembly; the retained table's CraneHole kicker sits at the far left, so this is a projection onto the crane mechanism rather than the drawn callout point.

Printed solenoid 04 is NOT USED: the Solenoid/Flasher Table lists the row with a driver transistor and a drive wire color but a blank Voltage Connections, Drive Connections, and Part Number column, and the Solenoid/Flashlamp Locations page prints item 04 Not Used with a blank assembly number. Enumerated-but-unfitted; no physical device is created.

Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 05 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: ScoopDown (Controller.Switch(72)=True, fork arms down). Projected onto the fork-lift scoop's left fork arm (P_Fork1, table object center): solenoid 5 (Scoop Down) drives the fork arms down and the retained script's ScoopDown handler rotates P_Fork1/P_Fork2, which sit at the scoop mechanism (agreeing with the manual's Solenoid Locations drawing, 'Right side, middle, at the scoop mechanism').
Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 06 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: BusDiverter (Sol6.IsDropped).
Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 07 (High Power). Retained script callback/driver: vpmSolSound SoundFX("Knocker",DOFKnocker).

Printed solenoid/flasher table entry 10 (Low Power). Retained script callback/driver: vpmSolSound SoundFX("Slingshot") left, PulseSwitch 51.
